options: Numerical representations of data that capture meaning, context or relationships in a form machines can understand
Compressed copies of raw text files
Encrypted versions of images
Relational tables that store words as symbols
Random numbers assigned to each record
questions.explanation: Embeddings are numerical representations of data that capture meaning, context or relationships in a form machines can understand. They convert words, images or other data into vectors (lists of numbers) that preserve relationships.

questions.stem: In the context of embeddings, what is a vector?
options: A type of database index
A list of numbers
A keyword search query
A compressed image file
A rule for classifying text
questions.explanation: Embeddings convert data into vectors, which are lists of numbers. These numbers are generated so that similar items have embeddings that are mathematically close in vector space.

questions.stem: Which pair of words is given as an example of embeddings that would be close to each other in vector space?
options: Apple and car
Fish and bird
King and queen
Dog and fish
Cheap and expensive
questions.explanation: The words 'king' and 'queen' have embeddings that are close to each other, whereas 'apple' and 'car' are farther apart. The distance between embeddings represents similarity.

questions.stem: In data architecture, where are embeddings often stored so that similarity search can be performed?
options: In spreadsheets
In relational tables of raw text
In email archives
In vector databases
In object storage as image files
questions.explanation: Embeddings are often stored in vector databases, where similarity search is performed using mathematical distance measures.

questions.stem: How does an embedding-based search differ from a traditional keyword search when a user searches for 'cheap running shoes'?
options: It returns only exact matches of the phrase
It ignores the query and shows popular products
It translates the query into another language
It searches only product images
It understands that 'affordable sneakers' may mean the same thing even though the words differ
questions.explanation: A traditional keyword system looks only for exact word matches. An embedding-based system captures semantic similarity, so it understands that 'affordable sneakers' may mean the same as 'cheap running shoes'.

questions.stem: In the Grade 7 animal example of embeddings, why are dog and wolf considered similar?
options: Because their number sets, such as [0.8, 0.6, 0.7] and [0.82, 0.59, 0.72], are close to each other
Because they have the same name length
Because they both live in water
Because their numbers are as different as possible
Because fish and birds were placed next to them
questions.explanation: Each animal is assigned numbers based on features such as size, habitat and behaviour. Dog [0.8, 0.6, 0.7] and wolf [0.82, 0.59, 0.72] have close numbers, so they are similar, while fish [0.1, 0.9, 0.2] is very different.

questions.stem: Conceptually, what does each dimension of an embedding's multi-dimensional space capture?
options: A single letter of the original word
A certain pattern learned from large amounts of data
The file size of the original data
The date the data was created
The name of the storage system
questions.explanation: Conceptually, every word or object is placed in a multi-dimensional space where each dimension captures a certain pattern learned from large amounts of data. Items close together in that space are semantically related.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a use of embeddings?
options: Similarity search
Clustering
Encrypting passwords
Classification
Retrieval-based generation
questions.explanation: Embeddings allow systems to perform similarity search, clustering, classification and retrieval-based generation, and are used in search engines, recommendation systems, chatbots and NLP. Encrypting passwords is not one of their uses.

questions.stem: What does an image embedding capture, compared with an audio embedding?
options: Both capture the file name
An image embedding captures sound characteristics; an audio embedding captures visual patterns
Neither captures anything beyond raw pixel or sample values
An image embedding captures visual patterns; an audio embedding captures sound characteristics
Only text can have embeddings
questions.explanation: The same principle applies to text, images and audio. An image embedding captures visual patterns, and an audio embedding captures sound characteristics.

questions.stem: How do embeddings enable AI systems to combine text and image understanding?
options: By storing both as plain keywords
By converting images into text descriptions only
By keeping each modality in a separate system that never interacts
By ranking images by file size
By converting different modalities into vectors so systems can compare them mathematically
questions.explanation: Embeddings are central to AI systems that combine text and image understanding. By converting different modalities into vectors, systems can compare them mathematically.
